title: 第171章 天地不公
text:
Grey Sixth told Hua Jiunan none of it — none of the bitterness, none of the years.

He only thought it to himself, quietly:

It's all past now.

The Little Master has shown us mercy, we of his household. No more going door to door like a dog with no master, tail between its legs, getting chased off porches with brooms. No more of those looks people give you that say you're not fit to stand on their ground......

For his part, Hua Jiunan had already made Grey Sixth an elder brother in his heart, blood or no blood. So he didn't stand on ceremony.

He took the Daoist manual, flipped through it once, and the basics recorded inside were his.

"Sixth Brother, I've got it all. Here's your book back."

"The younger ones in the family will be able to train off it someday. Good for laying a foundation."

"It's incomplete, though."

"If the chance ever comes, we ought to find the second volume and finish it."

Grey Sixth was still sunk in old memories, and it showed — a heaviness sat on his face like weather. He nodded slowly, took the manual back, and tucked it away against his chest with a carefulness he'd never shown anything he owned.

Hua Jiunan read him wrong. He read that heaviness, and it moved him.

He thought for a moment, then spoke.

"Sixth Brother — the breathing exercises, the breath-circulation, the Dragon-Tiger Binding I mean to teach you. You can pass all of it down to our sons and nephews. Every generation—"

He never finished.

The weight came down.

Not wind. Not thunder. Just weight — sudden and total, as if the sky had lowered itself three feet and set its palm on the crown of every head in the clearing. Zhao Fei felt it worst of all at first, being only a man; his chest heaved against air that had gone solid, his lungs unable to open all the way.

"We were fine a second ago — the hell is this......"

Chang Baye didn't say a word. Didn't think. His body simply folded inward, head buried in his own middle, the way a field mouse curls up when a hawk's shadow crosses the grass. Nothing to do with him. He knew nothing about anything.

Chen Daji opened his mouth to run it — and Grey Sixth clamped a hand over it.

"You little wretch, one more word and you're dead!"

Then, fast, bowing toward Hua Jiunan: "Little Master — the mercy you've shown my Grey family, we will carry it to our graves! But our blessings are shallow. Our spiritual reserves cannot bear such weight. We would never dare dream of carrying the Celestial Master's sacred canon down through the generations — please, take back what you just said!"

That was what his mouth said.

His face said something else entirely, and Hua Jiunan saw all of it — the thick grievance, the dejection, the loss. A man who had spent so long looking up at people that kindness from above still felt like a hand reaching down to pat his head.

What does a man live for?

Simply put — isn't it this: to see your family, your brothers, the ones you love, happy?

Looking at Grey Sixth's face, a fury rose in Hua Jiunan that reached for the sky.

He had already guessed where the pressure came from. It didn't matter. He dragged his head up against the weight, slow as pulling through deep water, and raised three fingers toward the black night — three fingers, a small pale hand against all that infinite dark, the way a man points when he swears an oath before a magistrate.

Only this magistrate was the sky itself.

"Three feet above my head, the gods are watching — I know you're there."

"Heaven and Earth, bear witness: Grey Sixth Brother has stood by me with his whole heart. He has gone into death for me, more than once!"

"The old law says: a man who does not repay kindness is no man at all. I have carried that law my whole life."

"I offer my own yin merit, my own allotted lifespan, as the price — so that in every generation of the Grey family, three may train in the arts I pass down!"

The air around his fingertips went grey, as if the years were already being drawn out of him.

Grey Sixth couldn't bear it. He hit the ground with a thud, kneeling.

"Little Master — your kindness to us is an ocean deep! My Grey family will remember it generation upon generation, not one second forgotten! But this we cannot accept — please, please take back your words!"

And then he pressed his forehead to the earth, and raised it, and pressed it down again. Bone on packed dirt. Again. Again. A rhythm with no prayer in it — only the mechanical desperation of a man trying to unsay what could not be unsaid. The dirt darkened where his brow struck. Mud worked into his fur.

The rats came out of hiding.

They poured from cracks in the earth, from under stones, from root-hollows — a dozen small grey bodies moving with terrible purpose. They ringed themselves around Hua Jiunan and Grey Sixth, stood up on their hind legs, pressed their front paws together in the old human gesture of supplication, and turned their faces upward. Black bead-eyes shining wet. Looking at the sky. Begging it. Claws scraping softly on the dirt, a whole family on its hind feet, pleading for permission to learn.

The weight kept growing.

Zhao Fei went down — flat on his stomach, breathing in shallow pulls.

Chen Daji didn't understand what was happening. But he understood someone was bullying Hua Jiunan and Grey Sixth Brother. The fool was rough as a fence post and dumb as one too, but he had never once lacked the guts to die for a friend.

He stood up into the pressure — shoulders shaking, legs bowed, standing anyway — pointed one finger at the sky, and cursed.

"Goddammit! What do you think you're doing? Picking on folks, is that it?"

"My grandmother used to say — the worst a man can do to you is put your head in the dirt. That's IT. That's all you got?"

"Grey Sixth Brother is kowtowing to you! What more do you want?!"

Still cursing, he hauled Grey Sixth up off the ground by the arm.

The two of them planted themselves behind Hua Jiunan, side by side, feet set.

"Sixth Brother, up! We're up!"

"Begging him's no use — fine, then we fight the son of a bitch!"

"To hell with the whole lot of it! If I'm gonna die, I'm gonna die standing, chest out and chin up — so go ahead, do your worst!"

Then Chen Daji drew back his fist and drove it into his own nose — hard, deliberate, like a man drawing a weapon. Blood burst across his upper lip and he didn't wipe it. He pulled a slingshot from his pocket — a child's toy, a forked stick and a rubber band — stretched the band taut, and aimed it at the sky.

And Grey Sixth, burned through by the fool's courage, with all the old years of grievance rising in him at once, threw back his head and howled:

"Heaven and Earth are unjust! Fate is unjust! MY GREY FAMILY DOES NOT SUBMIT!!!"
